items.title: Best no-capital farm
body: Complete Waystones quickly, sell raw currency and liquid map inputs, and use one low-interruption mechanic.

items.title: Best general rule
body: Choose a loop your build completes reliably and your trade routine can liquidate. Theoretical value that stays in a stash is not profit.

items.title: When to buy investment
body: After a baseline batch proves stable completion and after you define the exact sellable output the investment is meant to increase.

items.title: What should I record?
body: Starting cost, completed maps, failures, saleable returns, time spent mapping, and time spent pricing or trading.

sections.title: How to use this guide
paragraphs: Currency farming has three separate skills: clearing the content, converting rewards into liquid stacks, and protecting the bankroll from bad variance. A strategy is suitable only when all three work for the same character and player.

Patch 0.5 changes mechanics, Atlas Masters, and market demand, so this guide avoids fixed divines-per-hour promises. Use the matrices to select a repeatable loop, then test current prices before buying a large batch of inputs.

sections.title: Practical workflow
sections.intro: Run the process in order and preserve a rollback point before spending heavily.

cards.title: Step 1
body: Choose one output that has current buyers, then identify the mechanic and Atlas nodes that produce it.

cards.title: Step 2
body: Set aside the character-upgrade budget. Only the remaining currency is farming capital.

cards.title: Step 3
body: Run a baseline batch without expensive inputs and record total active time and deaths.

cards.title: Step 4
body: Add one investment layer, repeat the same batch, and compare net—not gross—returns.

cards.title: Step 5
body: Bulk-list liquid stacks at planned intervals; do not interrupt every map for a small sale.

cards.title: Step 6
body: Stop or downgrade the farm when completion, liquidity, or bankroll falls below the written limit.

sections.title: Common mistakes and fixes
sections.intro: These failures cost more time than a small difference between two reasonable choices.

cards.title: Counting listed value
body: Why it fails: Items may never sell at the displayed price.
Do this: Use completed sales or conservative bulk prices.

cards.title: Ignoring downtime
body: Why it fails: Price checks, stash sorting and trades reduce hourly output.
Do this: Use dump tabs and fixed liquidation windows.

cards.title: Buying too many inputs
body: Why it fails: A patch or price change can trap the bankroll.
Do this: Scale from small batches and keep a reserve.

cards.title: Farming a mechanic the build fails
body: Why it fails: High theoretical reward cannot compensate for lost maps.
Do this: Select by completion rate before peak value.

items.question: Which strategy makes the most currency?
answer: The one with the best net realised return for your completion speed, capital and trade tolerance; there is no permanent universal winner.

items.question: Should I sell or use valuable inputs?
answer: Sell them until your own tested return from using them exceeds the reliable sale price.

items.question: How do I avoid market manipulation?
answer: Compare multiple live listings, exclude obvious outliers, and value rare items only after a real sale.

items.question: Can solo players use bulk strategies?
answer: Yes. Standardise map preparation and sell in larger stacks at scheduled intervals.

items.question: When should I stop a bad batch?
answer: At the predetermined loss or failure limit, not after chasing the next lucky drop.
